name: Eaton
description: Eaton, an Irish-domiciled company with US operations, makes electrical equipment (switchgear, circuit breakers, power distribution and backup power, modular power enclosures) and sells it to data centres, utilities, industrial plants and buildings, plus aerospace fluid and power systems and truck and car powertrain parts. The two Electrical segments are about 73% of sales and about 79% of segment profit, with North American Electrical at a 29.9% margin. It is exiting the vehicle-powertrain side: on 2026-06-10 it agreed to combine its Mobility business with Dana in a tax-free Reverse Morris Trust.

employees.note: About 97,000 employees globally; 32,915 (33.8%) in the US per the 10-K table.

businessLines.name: Electrical Americas
businessLines.how: Sells electrical components, power distribution and assemblies, circuit protection, power quality, residential products and services produced and sold mainly in North and South America; mostly one-time equipment orders plus services. The 10-K lists data-centre, utility, industrial, commercial and residential among Eaton-wide markets.

businessLines.name: Electrical Global
businessLines.how: Same kind of electrical components, power distribution and assemblies, power quality and services, produced and sold primarily outside the Americas; one-time equipment plus services.

businessLines.name: Aerospace
businessLines.how: Supplies aerospace fuel, hydraulic and pneumatic systems and controls for commercial and military aircraft (20% of segment sales to three large aircraft makers); the 10-K does not split original-equipment from aftermarket sales.

businessLines.name: Vehicle
businessLines.how: Sells transmissions, clutches, hybrid power systems, superchargers and engine valves to car, truck and commercial-vehicle makers (37% of segment sales to four large vehicle makers); one-time component sales.

businessLines.name: eMobility
businessLines.how: Sells high-voltage inverters, converters, fuses, circuit protection and vehicle power distribution to on- and off-road vehicle makers (18% of segment sales to one vehicle maker); one-time component sales; roughly break-even in 2025.

brands.name: Fibrebond Corporation
brands.note: Acquired 2025-04-01 for $1.43 billion net of cash; modular power enclosures for data-centre, industrial, utility and communications customers; in Electrical Americas.

whatsNext.when: expected Q1 2027 (definitive agreements 2026-06-10; spin-off intent announced 2026-01-26)
whatsNext.text: Mobility business to be separated and combined with Dana in a tax-free Reverse Morris Trust; expected to close subject to Dana shareholder and regulatory approvals
